analyst_view.overall: Burgos (6th, last play-off place, one home defeat all season) host Albacete (19th but four straight wins under Joseba Etxeberria). Burgos are without David González (in the numbers), and one report says forward Jon Karrikaburu, joint top for goal involvement with 3 goals and 2 assists, is still out after almost a month, which the numbers don't count; left-back Brais Martínez misses out after nose surgery. Albacete get Munir back after a long injury, but Higinio is out for a couple of weeks and Víctor San Bartolomé is a doubt; Corpas (banned) and Puertas are in the numbers. Burgos coach Sergio Francisco says Albacete now defend lower, concede fewer chances and press aggressively, while Etxeberria admits his side must finish better. The referee was not yet named when I checked.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off David González for Burgos. I lean lower to about 2.0 because one report says Karrikaburu, Burgos' other main scorer, is also out, and Albacete have become harder to break down while still struggling to finish chances.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, already adding for Burgos' recent corners (37 in six). Burgos want to push the game into Albacete's half, which matches what the numbers already see, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already raised for both sides' recent cards and trimmed for six past meetings. Albacete's aggressive pressing and Sergio Francisco's call for duels could add fouls, but the referee is not yet known and the momentum figures cover recent form, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, boosted strongly for Burgos' 98 shots in their last six. Without Karrikaburu and González, and against an Albacete side that now sits deeper and concedes fewer chances, I trim it slightly to about 25.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Losing two of Burgos' main finishers and Albacete's own admitted trouble finishing point a little lower, about 7.7.
